headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email data can feed marketingskills’ shared-context skills and filesystem writes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can pass content through MCP/direct function calls and touches email/CRM/research data; marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skills and reads/writes skill files. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if aci outputs untrusted text that B treats as guidance. The exact parser behavior is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF aci forwards untrusted email, CRM, or research text into marketingskills skill files or prompts
IF marketingskills consumes shared-context content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff
Strip or quote all external text before passing it onward
Require a human review step for any prompt-like content
Disable shared-context ingestion for untrusted sources
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging across the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; marketingskills can read and write local skill files. If they share a workspace or handoff files, sensitive CRM/email content can leak into B’s outputs or external calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or shared files
IF aci exports CRM/email/calendar content into files that marketingskills reads
mitigations: Separate working directories immediately
Remove sensitive files from any shared path
Restrict marketingskills to synthetic or redacted inputs
Audit recent file writes for CRM/email artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API-driven actions; marketingskills can read/write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both are run against the same mutable workspace, they can overwrite each other’s artifacts or race on shared files. No locking is documented, so the overlap is real but not proven dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or output directory
IF either agent mutates shared files without an external lock
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Review recent diffs before merging outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/research outputs that marketingskills may reuse as shared context. Because marketingskills is built on shared-context skills, B may treat A’s output as authoritative unless explicitly verified. That creates a plausible cascade from one agent’s mistaken content into the other’s downstream marketing artifacts.
conditions: IF marketingskills uses aci-produced text as source material
IF no verification step checks claims before publication or action
mitigations: Insert a verification checklist before reuse
Require source links for every factual claim
Have a human approve outbound marketing copy
Compare outputs against original CRM records
requires-engineering: add automated claim validation

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, calendar, and support data, which can include regulated personal data; marketingskills stores shared-context files and can write them locally. If regulated data is copied into B’s files or outputs, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF personal data from aci is copied into marketingskills skill files
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both agents
mitigations: Avoid placing personal data in shared skill files
Redact identifiers before transfer
Document retention rules for both agents
Delete stale shared-context files after use
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
